newsitem.title: CHILE: RTRS-Codelco sees copper market surplus until 2000.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Codelco sees copper market surplus until 2000.

text.p: The world copper market is in oversupply which should last until 2000, an executive of Chile's state copper company Codelco said Friday.

"Starting in 1996, the market has moved back into a phase of oversupply which will probably last until the year 2000. From 2001 onward, we expect the market situation to turn around yet again," Codelco's assistant manager for research and strategic management Enrique Silva told a copper conference in Chile.
He said Codelco foresees world refined copper consumption growing by 2.6 percent a year from 1994 to 2000, but copper supply growth will be even faster and stocks will rise.

"Stocks, measured in terms of weeks of consumption, will increase from 4.4 weeks in 1995 to eight weeks in 1999, before dropping again to 6.6 weeks towards the year 2002," he said. "What this means is that over the next five years we expect the copper price, in constant currency, to remain below its average long-term equilibrium level. Nevertheless, this is a cyclical phenomenum that will tend to revert toward 2001."
Codelco plans to play its part in increasing world copper output and hold onto its western world market share of 15 percent of production.
"To do this, our goal is to produce over 1.5 million metric tonnes of copper by the year 2000," he added.
The state-owned firm is also embarked on a drive to reduce its cash cost to $0.435 cents a pound by 2000.
The company's $3.35 billion 1994-1999 investment plan will go 65 percent on project spending, including the expansion of the Andina mine, and the construction of the Radomiro Tomic oxides project.
